transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27 09:32 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Tessera Head of Partnerships), Tom (Tessera Enterprise Sales), Priya (Tessera Solutions Arch)

--- Summary (auto-gen - may be partial) ---
We covered who owns what in the co-sell funnel, agreed next steps for pricing and pilot onboarding, discussed risk areas: VPC timing, SOC2 evidence, SSO mapping. Agreed to run 2 pilot POCs (Aquila Health + one shadow account), share pricing spreadsheet and schedule kickoff.

--- Topics ---
1) Co-sell responsibilities and crediting
2) Pilot scoping and success metrics
3) Technical pre-reqs for Private/VPC deployment
4) Deal economics and partner margins
5) Pipeline cadence and scoreboard

--- Action items (from conversation) ---
- Jordan: partner playbook + pricing spreadsheet
- Maya: pilot runbook and benchmark checklist
- Luis: establish scoreboard + calendar invites
- Priya (Tessera): target account list

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumpin' on time. um quick roll call — real quick name and role?
[00:06] Aisha: Aisha Khan, Head of Partnerships at Tessera. excited to dig in.
[00:09] Tom: Tom Bradford, enterprise sales, will be running the pilot side from our team.
[00:12] Priya: Priya Nair, solutions architecture, I'll be the technical lead.
[00:15] Maya: Maya Chen, Redwood SE — I'll do the deep tech part, run the POC setup.
[00:19] Luis: Luis Romero, CSM Redwood — I'll own cadence and scoreboard ops.
[00:22] Jordan: Okay awesome. Agenda — align on co-sell play, pick two pilot accounts, agree on pricing bands and lead crediting. Any additions?
[00:30] Aisha: nope that's good. for context, Tessera has a couple of channel-sourced opportunities where the buyer is very sensitive about on-prem or VPC requirements plus SSO.
[00:38] Jordan: perfect, that's actually our sweet spot. quick question on your end: how much of these opportunities are already in pipeline vs new outreach?
[00:45] Tom: About 60% are existing ABM accounts, we have exec folks in intro. two accounts we want to prioritize — Aquila Health and Nautilus Financial. Aquila needs a HIPAA mapped solution.
[00:56] Priya: On Aquila — their security team will want SOC2 type II evidence, SAML SSO, and ideally a KMS integration for key management. they also want audit logs retained for 2 years.
[01:10] Maya: quick note on KMS — we integrate with major cloud KMS providers, and our private deployment has HSM/KMS options. we'll have to check retention policy but audit logs and export are supported in our console.
[01:22] Tom: timeline wise Aquila is looking to close procurement by mid-October. is that realistic?
[01:27] Jordan: it's tight but doable. depends on VPC provisioning time and how long your security review takes — we've seen 4–6 week cycles for enterprise SOC checks.
[01:35] Aisha: okay, so what are the steps to accelerate?
[01:38] Maya: First, baseline: we do a lightweight security pack (SOC artifacts, architecture diagrams, SSO integration docs). second, a constrained pilot — we can run a short 2-week technical evaluation in a dedicated VPC with sample data. third, if that passes, we move to procurement.
[01:52] Priya: would Redwood host the private control plane or would Tessera run the private on behalf of Aquila?
[01:57] Jordan: we usually offer two options — Redwood Private where the control plane can live in a customer-managed VPC, or a dedicated instance we host but with strict network peering. for faster timelines sometimes customers pick our hosted-but-isolated approach to avoid provisioning delays.
[02:12] Tom: cost / margin question — Tessera needs a partner margin to justify the engineering hours. how flexible is pricing during pilot vs post-contract?
[02:20] Jordan: we have partner-tier discounts for pilots and then partner margin tiering post-contract. I'll share the spreadsheet but typical pilot discounts run 30–40% off retail, then we tier depending on committed capacity.
[02:33] Aisha: and lead crediting — when Tessera sources the lead, what does Redwood expect for credit? referral or co-sell?
[02:39] Jordan: good question. we can do first-touch credit if Tessera brings the opportunity and coordinates the customer intro, co-sell credit if we jointly manage the deal. we'll document specifics in the playbook.
[02:49] Luis: we'll also add a scoreboard field for 'lead source' and 'crediting type' so no ambiguity.
[02:54] Priya: technical question — for Aquila's PHI data are there constraints around KV cache or in-memory state? we need to be explicit about data-in-transit and data-at-rest.
[03:04] Maya: MV — few points: our runtime keeps KV cache in memory but we can configure encryption at rest and blank out logs for PHI. for the pilot we'll push sample tokens that are synthetic, and we can sign an NDA for any real samples.
[03:19] Tom: sounds reasonable. who's leading the security artifacts we need to hand to Aquila?
[03:24] Jordan: Maya will own the tech pack, I'll own the legal/security attachments with our security team. Luis will help coordinate.
[03:30] Aisha: ok moving to the pilot scope — you mentioned a 2-week window, what are success criteria?
[03:36] Maya: I'd say three technical gates: latency under 500ms p50 for typical payloads, successful SAML SSO auth flows, and PV validated model outputs across the validation prompt set. business gate: Tessera and Aquila agree outputs meet QA thresholds for 2 sample workflows.
[03:51] Priya: latency under 500ms p50 may be optimistic depending on sequence length and embedding calls. what's the recommended model/quantization?
[03:59] Maya: for latency-first pilots we suggest a quantized LLM variant with batching disabled for low concurrency. we'll recommend runtime knobs in the runbook.
[04:07] Tom: ok on the POC side who's responsible for customer slides and exec brief?
[04:11] Aisha: Tessera will handle the exec briefing and Redwood to provide a short one-pager for the tech and ops overview.
[04:17] Jordan: noted. next topic: pipeline cadence — we propose a biweekly sync and a shared scoreboard in Google Sheets or Notion.
[04:24] Luis: I can set that up, include pipeline stage, ARR potential, close probability, next step, owner. Also will add a 'risk' column for VPC/SSO blockers.
[04:33] Aisha: great. on incentives — Tessera asks for marketing co-funds for one joint event per quarter in Q4. is co-marketing budget available?
[04:42] Jordan: we have a small co-marketing fund for strategic partners; we can propose a joint webinar and demo credits. details in the partner playbook.
[04:50] Priya: one more technical item — is there a supported path for on-prem inference with HSM-backed KMS? Aquila's legal said they'd prefer keys in HSM.
[04:59] Maya: yes, our private offering supports HSM or cloud KMS depending on environment. specific HSM integrations may require additional validation but it's supported roadmap-wise.
[05:09] Tom: any notable competitors in these accounts? they mentioned ModelServeX in the RFP.
[05:14] Jordan: we saw ModelServeX, and MegaCloud AI is sometimes in the running — the main differentiator for us is predictable inference economics and strong private deployment options.
[05:23] Aisha: pricing aside, Tessera wants clarity on support — SLA levels, on-call, escalation. can Redwood provide 24x7 enterprise support or do we need to bundle a premium package?
[05:35] Jordan: for enterprise accounts we provide priority support packages as an add-on. SLA levels and response times are in the enterprise attachment. I'll include a short excerpt in the packet we share.
[05:44] Priya: for the pilot, what's the expected engineer lift from Tessera's side? Tom?
[05:49] Tom: minimal but we will have 1 Solutions Engineer involved and one security reviewer. we can commit ~2 days/week of effort from Tessera during the 2-week pilot.
[05:58] Maya: and Redwood will provide 2 SE days upfront to do the configuration and a runbook for self-service.
[06:04] Jordan: let's lock on account list — agreed pilots: Aquila Health and Nautilus Financial as backup?
[06:10] Aisha: yes Aquila is top priority; Nautilus is softer but good as a secondary. we also propose a shadow-witness account — 'Ceres Insurance' — to demo at the exec briefing.
[06:20] Luis: I'll add those three to the scoreboard and mark Aquila as sprint-1.
[06:24] Tom: timeline check: we will need contract review time. procurement for Aquila target mid-October — so the pilot should complete by end of September ideally.
[06:33] Jordan: working back, pilot kickoff first week of September. Maya, is that doable?
[06:37] Maya: yes, if we get the account contacts and security checklist by early next week we can prep infra and have the runbook ready.
[06:44] Priya: we'll push account contacts by Friday. resource question: how will Redwood handle telemetry and cost reporting for the pilot?
[06:52] Jordan: our console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, with per-route dashboards. for pilots we can provide a short exported report.
[06:59] Aisha: good, please include a sample report in the materials.
[07:03] Maya: will do. one more note — some transcript/notes: we occasionally see transcription errors in automated outputs — excuse the typos.
[07:09] (laughter)
[07:12] Jordan: wrapping — Recap: Jordan to send playbook + pricing sheet; Maya to prepare pilot runbook; Luis to create scoreboard + cadence; Priya/Tessera to deliver account list and contacts. booked biweekly sync starting 2026-09-08.
[07:26] Aisha: thanks all. any blockers?
[07:29] Tom: none from me.
[07:30] Priya: no blockers.
[07:31] Jordan: great. I'll ping security for SOC artifacts and include an exec one-pager.
[07:36] Luis: I'll set the first cadence invite.
[07:38] Aisha: thanks, talk soon.
[07:40] Jordan: bye everyone.

(Transcript ends — exported from Fireflies. Note: timestamps approximate; transcription may have word errors: e.g., K V cash instead of KV cache, Redwood Private sometimes shown as Redwood Privet, etc.)
